newsitem.title: INDIA: Sister Nirmala elected to succeed Mother Teresa.
newsitem.headline: Sister Nirmala elected to succeed Mother Teresa.

text.p: Sister Nirmala, a Hindu convert to Roman Catholicism, has been elected to succeed Mother Teresa as the leader of the Missionaries of Charity order, the office of the archbishop of Calcutta said on Thursday.
"Sister Nirmala has been elected as the successor of Mother Teresa," Archbishop Henry D'Souza's office said in a statement released to Reuters in the eastern Indian city.

"Sister Nirmala, M.C. (Missionaries of Charity) was elected almost unanimously as the new Superior General," the statement said. "Mother Teresa was present for the election and blessed Sister Nirmala."
Sister Nirmala has supervised the order's centres in Europe and the United States. She has more recently headed the order's contemplative wing, in which elite nuns dedicate their lives to meditation.
She was not one of the order's councillors-general and thus was considered a dark horse in the eight-week election process.
Mother Teresa, suffering from heart, kidney and lung ailments, had said she did not want to continue to lead the order she founded in 1948.
